data.title: Whisky, big-screen TV seized from Indonesian prison ‘villas’
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesian authorities raided a prison outside Jakarta on Wednesday where inmates have allegedly been paying to live in luxury, emptying several “villas” of furniture, bottles of alcohol and at least one big-screen TV.

data.title: Nagoya mayor says sorry for Asian Games 'inconveniences'
data.description: NAGOYA — Nagoya's mayor apologised to athletes on Wednesday for "inconveniences" at the Asian Games in the Japanese city following a string of complaints.

data.title: Lost shark becomes viral star in South Korea
data.description: SEOUL - A wayward shark has become an unlikely celebrity in South Korea, drawing massive crowds, earning plaudits from the local mayor and even moving the stock market.

data.title: Bangkok's oldest amusement park facing 6-month closure from flood damage
data.description: Bangkok's 118-acre Siam Amazing Park has announced a temporary six-month closure after nearly the entire complex suffered severe flood damage and has remained submerged for five days.

data.title: Big Bad Wolf marks 10 years in Thailand
data.description: Big Bad Wolf Books is marking a decade in Thailand with its biggest Bangkok Book Sale yet, turning more than 5,574m² across two floors of Platinum Pop, opposite CentralWorld, into a city-centre Book Hunt from Oct 2–13.

data.title: Singha R-SA & rescue networks expand flood relief across Bangkok, Rayong & Prachin Buri
data.description: Singha R-SA has continued providing assistance to flood victims for the fifth consecutive day, deploying teams across several areas of Bangkok and working with rescue networks to evacuate residents in Rayong and Prachin Buri provinces.

data.title: Man City might be biggest cheats sporting world has ever seen. What comes next?
data.description: HONG KONG — "Don't get me started on financial fair play," Vincent Kompany said, immediately after his Bayern Munich team had beaten Aston Villa in a pre-season friendly at Kai Tak Stadium last month.

data.title: India's fat dog vote goes viral
data.description: NEW DELHI - India's capital has gone to the dogs, as voters choose which of the city's chubbiest canines deserves to be crowned its fattest.

data.title: Floods across four regions, 40 fatalities
data.description: Ongoing floods have spread to cover about 2,700 square kilometres and have killed 40 people with the most affected areas being the Central Plains, government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said on Wednesday.

data.title: North Korean leader 'extremely obese': Seoul spy agency
data.description: SEOUL - North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is understood to be "extremely obese", Seoul's spy agency said Wednesday, citing its latest assessment of the reclusive leader's health.

data.title: New releases for your streaming pleasure: Sept 30-Oct 6
data.description: Looking for a title to binge-watch this weekend? Here's our pick!

data.title: Thai Airways suspends cargo intake from Oct 1-6 amid flood disruption
data.description: Thai Airways International has announced a temporary suspension of inbound, outbound and transit cargo acceptance at its cargo terminal at Suvarnabhumi Airport from Oct 1-6 due to flooding disrupting staff travel and warehouse operations.

data.title: Countdown begins to biggest-ever Rugby World Cup
data.description: SYDNEY — Rugby's biggest World Cup kicks off in 12 months with a record 24 teams clashing over six weeks in Australia, and ominous back-to-back champions South Africa are already staking their claim to another title.

data.title: 'No limits': Marathon world record holder Sawe chasing history
data.description: BERLIN — Sabastian Sawe, the first man to run the marathon in under two hours, believes even faster times are on the horizon both for him and the sport.

data.title: Malaysia's ex-PM Mahathir in hospital for observation
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia's 101-year-old former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad has been hospitalised for observation, his aide told AFP Wednesday, a day after the death of his wife of seven decades.

data.title: PM caught handing out cash to flood victims
data.description: Sparking online debate after being captured on a Facebook live stream , Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was seen handing out cash to flood-hit residents of communities in Bangkok's Sai Mai district late on Tuesday.

data.title: Bangkok's City Hall reports flooding on about 10 roads
data.description: The Drainage and Sewerage Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) reported flooding on about 10 roads in the capital on Wednesday morning, with water levels ranging from seven to 20 centimetres.

data.title: Bangkok opens shelter for animals rescued from floodwaters
data.description: Dogs and cats displaced by severe flooding in Bangkok can now receive temporary shelter, health assessments and medical care at the Prawet Animal Shelter, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) announced on Wednesday.

data.title: Radio waves coming from an alien planet may be a cosmic first
data.description: NEW YORK — Radio waves streaming from an alien planet may offer a new tool in the hunt for life elsewhere in the universe.

data.title: Thieves swipe drugs under nose of Fiji police, swap with flour
data.description: SYDNEY — Detectives were sifting leads Wednesday after a massive drug heist in Fiji, searching for dozens of cocaine parcels swiped from an evidence vault and replaced with baking flour.

data.title: Singha R-SA & Rescue Networks Expand Flood Relief Across Bangkok, Rayong & Prachin
data.description: Singha R-SA has continued providing assistance to flood victims for the fifth consecutive day, deploying teams across several areas of Bangkok and working with rescue networks to evacuate residents in Rayong and Prachin Buri provinces.

data.title: North Korea denies South's claim it was apparently behind DMZ mine blasts
data.description: SEOUL — The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un denied a South Korean claim that North Korea was apparently behind landmine blasts last week that injured three soldiers, state media reported Wednesday.

data.title: West Bank's violent settlers part of a new generation fuelled by ideology
data.description: JERUSALEM — A mass attack by Israeli settlers on a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank has placed new focus on the emergence of a generation of radicals in the territory.

data.title: Myanmar arrests 21 over alleged donations to opposition-linked fundraising platform
data.description: NAY PYI TAW — Myanmar's military-backed government has arrested 21 people it said ​had transferred money to an online ‌fundraising platform linked to the opposition National Unity Government (NUG), the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper reported.
